correctness.rationale: For all generic normals the origin-inside ring yields exactly two crossed ring edges. If apex signs differ, exactly n apex-ring edges cross; if they agree, 2r or 2(n-r) do. Antipodal regular-ring pairing gives n+2 vertices for even n; odd n gives exactly n+1,n+2,n+3. Independent Haar sphere latitude integration computes same-sign-apex weight lambda |cos psi|/sqrt(1+lambda^2 cos^2 psi). Odd-order angular alternation has elementary arcsine antiderivative, giving the finite exact distribution. For k=lambda/sqrt(1+lambda^2)<1, positive magnitudes of odd sine coefficients of arcsin(k sin psi) follow directly from the power series of arcsine and sine powers, and square-wave orthogonality proves strict difference and the exact lambda^n asymptotic. Rigorous limits and inverse parameter come from positive fixed-interval integrals. Hull-derived numerical verification, 18 x 85000 directions, quadrature and 70-digit small-shear tests executed successfully; numerical tests only corroborate the universal proof.

The 2024 full-text hyperplane slicing work classifies maximum section sizes and attainable counts, not shape-dependent distribution. Older stereological random-affine-plane formulas (Voss 1982) use an inequivalent sampling measure; complete text was unavailable and priority uncertainty remains. No inspected publication or retrieved research statement logically yields the full n-dependent finite arcsine law with strictly positive order-lambda^n imbalance.

value.rationale: This determines a complete naturally motivated cross-sectional probability distribution for all regular-base bipyramid orders under a nontrivial shear, including an even/odd rigidity transition, inverse recovery of the shear-to-height ratio from a single probability, strict one-sided imbalance, and a sharp high-order lambda^n symmetry cancellation. These are structural classifications rather than arbitrary small numerical cases. Their usefulness is intrinsic to geometric stereology of fixed-center sections; no paper-scale downstream theorem is claimed.
